Open a page of the project's dashboard in your browser, and print its address. Without a page, opens
the project's overview. Off a terminal, or with --no-browser, the address is only printed.

Pages: overview, products, product, perks, persons, person, flags, flag, experiments, experiment,
paywalls, paywall, locations, location, components, events, event-settings, analytics, ads,
ad-accounts, campaigns, creatives, cohorts, webhooks, webhook, providers, provider, keys,
notifications, settings, domains, sandbox, push.

product, person, flag, experiment, paywall, location, webhook and provider open the page of one
item, which you name after it or choose on a terminal.

Usage:
  voidhash open [page] [item] [flags]

Arguments:
  page  The dashboard page to open (default: overview)
  item  For product, paywall or location: its slug, name or id; for person: their email, distinct id
        or id; for flag: its key or id; for experiment: its name or id; for webhook: its name, URL
        or id; for provider: app-store, google-play, stripe or a payment source's slug

Flags:
  -h, --help               Show help for this command
      --no-browser         Only print the page's address
      --project <project>  Project to act on: its id, slug, organization/slug or name (default: this
                           directory's project, then your default project)

Global flags:
  -d, --debug              Print each request and full error detail to standard error
      --no-color           Print without colors (also when NO_COLOR is set)
      --profile <profile>  Use a named config profile: its settings override the base config
                           (default: VOIDHASH_PROFILE)

Examples:
  voidhash open
  voidhash open products
  voidhash open product pro-monthly
  voidhash open person ada@example.com --no-browser
